South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 78 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 01/14/26 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for COPD management, assessment of persistent lower extremity edema, and evaluation of worsening fatigue.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax presents for a follow-up visit, primarily focused on the management of his chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), persistent bilateral lower extremity edema, and deteriorating fatigue. He reports that while the addition of a nighttime albuterol inhaler has somewhat alleviated his nocturnal wheezing, he continues to experience significant daytime dyspnea, particularly with exertion, which has been exacerbated by recent colder weather.
The bilateral lower extremity edema remains a significant issue. Despite dietary sodium restrictions and adherence to furosemide, which remains at 80 mg daily, Mr. Fairfax notes that the edema has not diminished and is still noted as 1+ pitting, particularly after prolonged periods of sitting. He denies any associated symptoms such as pain or redness but expresses concern over the impact this condition has on his mobility and quality of life.
His fatigue has worsened, now described as debilitating, significantly affecting his daily activities and social interactions. He reports increased feelings of anxiety and depression, likely stemming from his ongoing health issues and lack of improvement in his symptoms.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + worsening fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + daytime dyspnea, + nocturnal wheezing, - cough, - sputum production, no hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain in knees and hands, no swelling. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, increased use to five times daily due to persistent symptoms. 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 1 puff twice daily. 4. Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaler, 1 puff daily. 5. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain. 6. Furosemide 80 mg daily.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.4F, HR 76, BP 128/82, RR 24, O2 sat 87% on room air
General: Elderly male in no acute distress but appears fatigued and anxious. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, moderate wheezing noted on expiration, no crackles. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 1+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 8.5, Hgb 12.0, Hct 35.5, Plt 220 2. BMP: Na 135, K 4.1, Cl 95, CO2 25, BUN 18, Cr 1.2, Glucose 90 3. BNP: 480 (slightly elevated). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 3.5 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: The patient continues to experience significant daytime dyspnea and nocturnal symptoms. Maintain the current regimen of tiotropium and fluticasone/salmeterol, but consider increasing the frequency of albuterol use. Discussed the potential benefits of pulmonary rehabilitation to improve exercise tolerance. Follow-up in 1 month for reassessment. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. Blood pressure remains stable. Follow-up in 1 month. 3. Lower extremity edema: The edema persists. Reinforce dietary sodium restrictions and encourage Mr. Fairfax to elevate his legs more frequently. Referral to nephrology will be arranged if no improvement is noted by the next follow-up. 4. Fatigue: Given the worsening fatigue and psychological concerns, continue the referral to a psychologist for evaluation and management of anxiety and potential depression. Schedule follow-up CBC and metabolic panel in one month to monitor for any changes.
Patient education reiterated regarding recognizing signs of exacerbation, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to effectively manage COPD and edema.
